latest_apis.rationale: Consistently on the current generation (Next 16 + React 19, async params, App Router conventions, no legacy router or experimental PPR flags). The one previous-model knob, `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` in all six routes, is load-bearing today for the spec's no-build-time-data rule but is slated for removal under Cache Components, which Next 16 stabilized and plans to make default. Source: nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config (v16.0.0 version history: dynamic/revalidate/fetchCache 'removed when Cache Components is enabled') and /docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents.

platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform first throughout: native fetch, URLSearchParams, Map/Set, padStart, localeCompare, native form controls and timers, and modern CSS (custom props, grid, :focus-visible). The only place a platform/framework primitive would be more idiomatic is the hand-rolled global promise cache (spec permits runtime caching, but React cache()/use cache or an LRU would be the maintained path).

dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: three deps, current majors, exact pins, and several places where a utility dependency would have been the lazy choice but wasn't taken. The missing devDependencies (eslint, typescript) are a tooling gap flagged below, not a dependency problem.

churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, formatting, and constants are well single-sourced and no framework internals are touched, so a minor-version upgrade is cheap. But the previous-model segment config is duplicated across all six routes (the one export Next will force you to delete), there are no types at the API boundary, and API record shapes leak into route components — so both a framework major and an upstream data change touch many files.

findings.location: app/app/page.js:17 (also moves/[name]/page.js:8, types/page.js:5, types/[name]/page.js:9, abilities/[name]/page.js:7, pokemon/[name]/page.js:10)
findings.issue: `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` is previous-model route segment config; Next 16 moved it out of the Route Segment Config reference into the 'Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)' guide and removes it entirely under the stabilized cacheComponents flag, which the docs say will be enabled everywhere in the next major release.
findings.suggestion: Drop it where a dynamic API (searchParams) already forces request-time rendering, and adopt `cacheComponents` for the rest — its dynamic-by-default data fetching matches the spec's live-data requirement exactly and would let the six exports be deleted rather than rewritten under protest.

findings.issue: No TypeScript and no JSDoc types anywhere: all PokeAPI responses are consumed through untyped optional-chained accesses (e.g. app/lib/api.js:59, app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.js:70-71), so upstream data-shape drift or a typo'd field name surfaces as a runtime rendering failure, not a build failure.
findings.suggestion: Migrate to tsconfig (or at minimum JSDoc typedefs for the resource records in lib/api.js with `checkJs: true`), which is the single biggest thing this codebase could do to age well.

findings.issue: Raw API record shapes (damage_relations, sprites.other['official-artwork'], varieties, learned_by_pokemon) are read directly inside route components, so a PokeAPI change touches pages in addition to lib/api.js.
findings.suggestion: Have lib/api.js return normalized view models (displayName, types[], damageRelations) so route components render shapes the app owns.

findings.issue: The filter-URL contract (q/type/generation param names and default-omission rules) is implemented twice, server-side in pageHref and client-side in Controls.apply (app/app/Controls.js:24), so a URL-shape change must be made in two places.
findings.suggestion: Extract one shared buildFilterUrl(filters, page) helper used by both the server pagination links and the client controls.

findings.issue: The global in-memory cache is unbounded: every species, pokemon, move, ability and version-group record ever requested is retained for process lifetime, which under production traffic on 1025 species plus move graphs grows into hundreds of MB.
findings.suggestion: Bound it (LRU with a byte/entry budget) or replace with `use cache` + `cacheLife` once Cache Components is adopted, which also gives revalidation hooks.

findings.issue: No devDependencies at all — no ESLint (Next 16 removed `next lint`, so linting must be wired by hand) and no typecheck, so nothing mechanically guards style or correctness drift.
findings.suggestion: Add eslint + eslint-config-next (flat config) and a lint/CI script; it's the cheapest guard for a codebase this clean.

findings.issue: The production build output directory sits inside app/ and the root .gitignore only covers /data/, /.data-cache/ and node_modules/, so build artifacts risk being committed.

Plain instead of next/image bypasses the image optimizer; defensible for an env-derived remote host and 96px sprites (and width/height/loading=lazy are correctly set), but it's a non-default choice a future maintainer will question.
findings.suggestion: Either note the rationale in a comment or configure images.remotePatterns and switch to next/image with `unoptimized` if optimizer cost is the concern.

summary: A genuinely current-generation Next 16 / React 19 app: async server components, correct async params handling, App Router conventions, and a three-dependency runtime with no bloat — the code is cleanly factored with all data access behind lib/api.js. Its one dated pattern is the previous-model `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` copied into every route, which is load-bearing today but will hard-error the moment the framework's stabilized-and-default-bound cacheComponents model lands. The other real aging risk is the total absence of types (and lint tooling) at the PokéAPI boundary, so upstream data drift fails only at runtime.

apis.api: metadata title template in root layout

apis.replacement: Cache Components model (cacheComponents: true): dynamic-by-default data fetching with `use cache`/`cacheLife` for anything you want cached; the export is removed (and errors) when cacheComponents is enabled. Source: nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config v16.0.0 version history and /docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components
next/image with images.remotePatterns is the framework default, but plain img is a valid deliberate choice for an env-configured remote host with tiny sprites
